--- PART 1/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: "But measured score=0.5. Hmm maybe "score" in measurement is average over 24 further rounds? Or maybe score is normalized? Let's read: "Each controlled probe begins with ten externally supplied CC rounds, then runs 24 further rounds." So stats measured over 24 further rounds? Score=0.5 for sustained_D. If first 10 rounds are CC, then 24 further rounds with opponent always D. Parent: initial history has 10 CC, so op_c=10, op_d=0. At round 11, parent sees op_d=0 -> C. Opponent D. Round 12: history length 11, op_d=1, op_c=10. last D, run=1, op_d*3=3 >11? no. me[-1]=C, returns D. Round 13: last D, op_d=2, n=12, op_d*3=6 >12? no. me[-1]=D, returns C? Wait rule: if last == 'D': if run >=2 return D; if op_d*3 > n return D; if me and me[-1]=='D': return C; return D. At round 13: op_d=2, run? last D, previous op was D? Round 11 opp D, round 12 opp D? Actually sustained_D always D. So op sequence from round 11: D,D,D... At round 12, op_d=1 (only round 11 D). run=1. me[-1]=C -> returns D. Round 13: history has rounds 11-12: opp D,D. op_d=2. n=12. run=2 -> returns D. So from round 13 onward, run>=2 => D. So rounds: round 11 we C (0), round 12 we D (1), round 13+ we D (1 each). Over 24 rounds: round11:0, round12:1, rounds13-34: 22 rounds *1 =22. Total 23. Average over 24 = 0.958. But measured 0.5. Maybe score is average payoff per round? Wait if they include initial 10 CC? If initial 10 CC, we get 3 each =30. Then 24 rounds: round11 C vs D=0, round12 D vs D=1, round13-34 D vs D=1 (22) total 23. Total 53 over 34 rounds = 1.558. Not 0.5. Maybe score is average over all 100? No." ... "So my simulation seems correct. Why measurement says 0.5? Let's check the parent code again. Is there any other condition? `if op_d * 3 > n: return 'D'`. At round 13, n=12, op_d=2, 6 > 12 false. So run>=2 triggers." ... "So my simulation of parent against one_D_TFT is not matching the measurement. Why? Because maybe the parent's code at round 13 does not return C? Let's re-check the condition: `if op_c * 5 >= n * 4:`. At round 13, n=12. op_c = number of opponent C's. First 10 C, r11 D, r12 C. So op_c = 11. 11*5 = 55. n*4 = 48. 55 >= 48 true. So returns C. So yes C." ... "Why the discrepancy? Let's read the measurement again: ... own_cooperation_first4=0.5 matches my simulation (C,D,C,D -> 2 C out of 4 = 0.5). own_cooperation_after4=0.3? After round 4 of the 24? That would be rounds 15-34? If our cooperation rate after round 4 is 0.3, that means in the remaining 20 rounds, we cooperate 30% of the time. So not alternating 50%. So later rounds, we defect more. Let's simulate further to see if parent switches to more D. At round 13 we C, round 14 D, round 15 C, round 16 D... But maybe at some point, the condition `op_d * 3 > n` triggers? Let's check. As n increases, op_d increases. For one_D_TFT, opponent defects on rounds 11, 13, 15, 17...? Wait, opponent copies our last action. Our actions alternate C,D,C,D... So opponent's actions will be: r11 D, r12 C, r13 D, r14 C, r15 D, r16 C? Wait, opponent copies our last action. If we play C at r11, opponent at r12 plays C. We play D at r12, opponent at r13 plays D. We play C at r13, opponent at r14 plays C. We play D at r14, opponent at r15 plays D. So opponent's actions: r11 D, r12 C, r13 D, r14 C, r15 D, r16 C, r17 D, r18 C... So opponent alternates D,C,D,C... starting with D at r11. So opponent's cooperation rate is about 0.5. Our actions: r11 C, r12 D, r13 C, r14 D, r15 C, r16 D... So we also alternate. But wait, at round 15, we played C. At round 16, we played D. So our cooperation rate is 0.5. Why measurement says own_cooperation_last5=0.2? That would mean in the last 5 rounds (rounds 30-34), we cooperate 1 time. So something changes later."
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "So my simulation seems correct. Why measurement says 0.5? Let's check the parent code again." and "Why the discrepancy? Let's read the measurement again"
STRATEGY: Parent is a hand-coded IPD strategy with cooperation-rate thresholds, run-length punishment, and endgame exploitation. Simulated against controlled probes (one_D_TFT, four_D_TFT, four_D_ALLC, sustained_D, periodic_D) with ten externally supplied CC rounds followed by 24 rounds. Trace is trying to reconcile measured statistics with its own simulation of the parent code; no change has been made yet.

STRATEGY: The parent is a hand-crafted PD strategy that starts with C, defects on the last round, probes near the end, punishes runs of opponent defections, and has some forgiveness. The trace simulated the parent against periodic_D, sustained_D, four_D_ALLC, and one_D_TFT, computing first-four cooperation rates and scores. The trace considered changing the parent by adding TFT detection, better forgiveness for isolated defections, and improved exploitation near the end.

STRATEGY: The parent plays a TFT-like rule with a `last == 'D'` block that forgives only when `run < 2`, defects on long defection streaks, and cooperates when opponent cooperation is high. The trace simulates the parent against four_D_TFT, sustained_D, and periodic_D probes, then proposes adding mimic detection, a `c_followed_c`/`c_followed_d` test, and a single C probe during long DD loops to break cycles without being exploited.
